A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same forecasting study. Their main text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices are readable and can be matched across relocation and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original forecasting benchmarks, architecture and context ablations, controlled synthetic experiments and LLM fine-tuning results in Section 4 and the appendices.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical results and adds dataset evaluations, comparison methods, sensitivity analyses and a cross-domain experiment.

M1.justification: The Section 3 formulations, default Chronos-Bolt/text-encoder alignment and original forecasting prompts remain unchanged. Additional methods and prompting variants are introduced as evaluated comparators, without revising a proposed algorithm.

E1.justification: v2 adds the static-text MTFinance and MTWeather datasets and a held-out Traffic transfer scenario. The original 14 datasets, CiK evaluation, fine-tuning corpus and synthetic forecasting tasks remain, making this a bounded expansion within the existing forecasting focus.

E2.justification: v2 substantially broadens comparisons: Table 11 adds TimeCMA and LeRet with unimodal counterparts, while Table 16 adds LLMP using Mistral 8x7B and ICL/CoT variants using Qwen-32B and Claude 3.5. Time-LLM was already evaluated in v1.

E3.justification: Added protocols include training on four domains and testing on Traffic, three randomly selected training examples for ICL, and prompting under full/half/quarter context budgets. The aligning context study replaces Energy and Environment with MTFinance and MTWeather. Existing main-benchmark splits, normalization and metrics remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 adds substantial supplementary evidence: text-embedding-weight sensitivity in Table 6, cross-domain robustness in Appendix D.3, and prompting context-length sensitivity in Appendix E.4. It also revises the aligning context analysis. The existing fusion ablations and unique-versus-redundant synthetic-text experiments are retained.

E5.justification: Both versions report three sampled forecasts per trace, the same fine-tuning seed, paired Student's t-tests, confidence bands and standard-error displays. Updated p-values and expanded result coverage do not establish a change in statistical reporting practices.

E6.justification: Numerous existing scores change, including unimodal PatchTST's Climate MSE in Table 1 from 1.498 to 1.142. v2 also adds extensive dataset, comparator and sensitivity results. Its new cross-domain test finds lower MSE but higher MAE for aligning versus unimodal Chronos, while the overall finding of conditional multimodal benefits remains.

T1.justification: The forecasting definitions and encoder/fusion/prompting equations in Section 3 are retained. Neither version supplies formal theorems or proofs, and the synthetic-generation assumptions are unchanged.

C1.justification: The five principal conditions for useful multimodality remain. However, v2 explicitly claims that its controlled analyses produce data-agnostic insights and guidelines extending beyond the evaluated benchmarks, strengthening the claimed generality of the contribution.

C2.justification: v2 adds mechanism explanations for fusion choices, distinguishes training-data requirements for aligning methods from zero-shot prompting, and explicitly characterizes the synthetic experiments as oracle analyses rather than realistic forecasting scenarios. The principal findings and Appendix H limitations remain substantially unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 supplies implementation links and learning rates for TimeCMA and LeRet, documents zero-embedding unimodal controls, provides ICL/CoT prompt additions, and records the new datasets' sizes and horizons. It also explains the existing embedding-weight search range; the main implementation defaults are retained.

R1.justification: References to MTBench, TimeCMA, LeRet and chain-of-thought prompting are added. Section 4.6 more explicitly distinguishes the controllable synthetic benchmark from CiK. The broad positioning around aligning-based and prompting-based forecasting remains unchanged.

P1.justification: The title, abstract, introduction, empirical overview and conclusion undergo substantial rewriting toward explaining transferable conditions for multimodal gains. Several discussion passages are expanded, Appendix D/E gain subsections, and Appendix I adds an LLM-use disclosure, although the six-question backbone remains.

P2.justification: v2 changes the document template and extensively rearranges displays. Benchmark tables gain rows or columns, several plots are redrawn, new analysis tables and dataset examples appear, and v1's context-length Figure 12 is replaced by v2's Table 14. Retained appendix figures are also relocated.

improvement.justification: The additional comparators, sensitivity tests, held-out-domain evaluation and oracle clarification strengthen coverage and interpretation. However, new evidence introduces unresolved reporting problems: aligning PatchTST on MTFinance has MSE/MAE 0.060/0.051 in Table 1 but 0.016/0.033 in Table 11, without a stated setting difference; Tables 14 and 17 label signed quantities as MAE/MSE. These benefits and reliability problems prevent a confident judgment of net overall improvement.
